articles.headline: Rams place kicker Blake Grupe on IR due to knee injury
articles.description: The Rams have placed kicker Blake Grupe on injured reserve after he injured his right knee in the team's Week 6 loss to the Cardinals.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- The Los Angeles Rams have placed kicker Blake Grupe on injured reserve after he injured his right knee in the team's Week 6 loss to the Arizona Cardinals, the team announced Monday.

The Rams have not announced a corresponding move at kicker.

Grupe was playing in his first game with Los Angeles after he was signed off the New York Jets' practice squad last week. Grupe was signed to replace Harrison Mevis, who missed a 50-yard field goal attempt and then had a 48-yarder blocked in overtime of the Rams' Week 5 loss to the Buffalo Bills.

But after making a 44-yard field goal in the opening quarter Sunday, Grupe hurt his right knee on the ensuing kickoff while trying to make a tackle. After the game, Grupe was in the locker room with a big brace on his right leg and crutches at his locker.

The Rams play the Raiders in Las Vegas in Week 7.

articles.headline: NFL suspends Bills' C.J. Gardner-Johnson for one game for spitting
articles.description: The NFL has suspended Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson for one game after cameras captured him spitting toward Raiders players on Sunday.
articles.body:
The NFL has suspended Buffalo Bills safety C.J. Gardner-Johnson for one game without pay after cameras captured him spitting toward Las Vegas Raiders players on Sunday.

The league said in a statement that Gardner-Johnson violated Rule 12, Section 3, Article 1, which applies to "any act which is contrary to the generally understood principles of sportsmanship."

Barring an appeal, Gardner-Johnson will miss the Bills' Week 8 game against the Baltimore Ravens. Buffalo is on a bye this week. Any appeal would be heard by Derrick Brooks, Jordy Nelson, Ron Rivera or James Thrash, who are jointly appointed and paid by the NFL and the NFL Players Association.

Bills coach Joe Brady said Monday there'll be no further punishment for Gardner-Johnson beyond the league's suspension. Brady remained committed to Gardner-Johnson as a starter when he's eligible to return from suspension in Week 9.

"C.J. knows that it's hard enough to win in this league with 48 guys, much less 47. He knows that that can't happen. It's inexcusable. That's not the standard that we're going to have and play with. He's addressed it. It's been addressed. The league came down with the suspension. ... We want to toe the line with everything we do but we can't cross the line."

Brady preferred to keep the conversations between he, Gardner-Johnson and the team private. Even given Gardner-Johnson's reputation for toeing and crossing the line, Brady said he has no problem with Gardner-Johnson's personality or character fit within the organization, saying he doesn't need all of his players to behave in one prescribed way.

"We brought him here for a reason," Brady added. "He knows he has to play better, and he knows he has to be better for this team. Just like everybody else we've got to learn from this stuff, and we have to improve and find ways to get better as the season goes."

Gardner-Johnson was ejected from Sunday's game after spitting in the direction of Raiders tight end Brock Bowers and center Tyler Linderbaum shortly before halftime. He apologized to his teammates after the Bills' 33-30 victory and said he needed to be a better veteran moving forward.

The incident came after a play in which Gardner-Johnson and Bowers jawed, but Gardner-Johnson said there wasn't a specific incitement that sparked the flagrant act.

"We were just arguing and talking," Gardner-Johnson told reporters. "It was nothing negative. He ain't do nothing to me. It was just in the heat of the game arguing and talking s---. That gesture isn't warranted."

Said Bowers: "I don't even know. Just talking a little bit and then ... I don't know."

Later Sunday, in a social media post, Gardner-Johnson formally apologized "to my opponent, my teammates, my organization, and everyone who supports me."

articles.headline: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts' blood clot diagnosis explained
articles.description: ESPN spoke with a medical professional for a better understanding of causes, treatments and outlook for those with blood clots.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 NFL season after doctors discovered multiple blood clots in his lungs, sources told NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter.

Hurts will undergo treatment involving blood thinners that is expected to sideline him for at least three months, sources informed of the diagnosis told Rapoport and Schefter.

Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, and the Eagles released a statement Monday detailing Hurts' condition. Lynn and the Eagles said Hurts has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, meaning a blood clot traveled from his leg to his lungs.

Hurts was originally diagnosed with having a superficial blood clot, according to a team statement released on Oct. 15, which was discovered following an ultrasound in London before the Eagles' Week 5 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. It was deemed that mobility was important and Hurts could safely play in the game, per the statement. A follow-up ultrasound last Wednesday showed the blood clot had moved, the team said. Hurts was subsequently ruled out of Sunday's Week 6 game against the Carolina Panthers and has since been put on injured reserve.

ESPN spoke with Dr. Jordan K. Schaefer, associate professor of internal medicine at the University of Michigan specializing in disorders of hemostasis and thrombosis, for a better understanding of causes, treatments, and outlook for those with blood clots. Dr. Schaefer has not treated Hurts and is not involved with the Eagles.

The conversation has been edited for brevity and clarity.

Jalen Hurts is going to have to go on anticoagulants because he has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli. What should we know about that?

Schaefer: About one out of four people presenting with a superficial vein thrombosis, which is a blood clot that is in the veins closer to the skin of the leg, will also have a deep vein thrombosis, which is in the deeper vein system.

When we're initially evaluating a superficial vein thrombosis, we will often do an ultrasound to look at a few things. The things that we're really looking for are, is there a deep vein thrombosis at the time that you're diagnosing the superficial vein thrombosis? What is the size of the superficial vein thrombosis, and how close is that superficial vein clot to the deep vein system? And that kind of lets us know the risk of the superficial blood clot and how to approach the initial management. We'll also be talking to patients about symptoms that could suggest a pulmonary embolism, and a pulmonary embolism occurs when a blood clot travels through the bloodstream and into the pulmonary arteries of the of the lung. The reason we are cautious about superficial blood clots is they can extend into the deep vein system, where they're then at higher risk for traveling to the lungs and causing a potentially serious event of a pulmonary embolism.  Deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism are the feared thing

articles.headline: Warriors expect Steph Curry (ankle) to play in opener vs. Lakers
articles.description: The Warriors expect Stephen Curry to be available for Wednesday night's season opener against the Lakers despite tweaking his right ankle during an open scrimmage Sunday.
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors expect Stephen Curry to be available for Wednesday night's season opener against the Los Angeles Lakers despite tweaking his right ankle during an open scrimmage Sunday afternoon.

Curry was a full participant in practice Monday morning, and Warriors coach Steve Kerr said Curry reassured him he was "fine" soon after leaving the floor in clear discomfort.

Curry rolled his ankle on a dribble move from the right wing midway through the scrimmage. After the misstep, he stopped action, banged the basketball on the floor and limped to the locker room in front of a concerned arena of teammates and fans. He didn't return to the scrimmage.

But Curry's ankle responded well overnight, and the medical staff cleared him to continue his ramp-up to the regular season, expecting him to play against the Lakers on Wednesday after another practice Tuesday.

Curry will turn 39 in March. He spent the summer reconfiguring his routine to better manage a persistent right knee problem that forced him to miss 27 games last season. The Warriors were careful with his preseason minutes, and Kerr said they will have him practice less to ease his workload.

The Warriors are already without starting wings Moses Moody and Jimmy Butler III, both rehabbing serious knee injuries and expected back midseason.

Starting center Kristaps Porzingis remains out indefinitely with a private health issue and won't travel to Los Angeles with the team. Starting guard Brandin Podziemski missed Monday's practice with lower back tightness and is questionable for the opener.

articles.headline: Colts to stick with Daniel Jones at quarterback vs. Vikings
articles.description: Daniel Jones will remain the Indianapolis Colts' starting quarterback when they travel to play the Minnesota Vikings in Week 7, coach Shane Steichen said.
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS -- Daniel Jones will remain the Indianapolis Colts' starting quarterback when they travel to play the Minnesota Vikings in Week 7, coach Shane Steichen said.

Jones' status has been a question amid his continued struggles, the Colts' stunning loss to the Tennessee Titans on Sunday and Monday's firing of general manager Chris Ballard.

Jones has committed nine turnovers this season, second only to Los Angeles Chargers' quarterback Justin Herbert. He also ranks near the bottom of the league's starting quarterbacks in many of the major passing categories, including QBR (30th), completion rate (29th) and yards per attempt (29th).

But Steichen, who has consistently defended his quarterback, said no change at the position was planned.

"He's aware that he has to produce and play better," Steichen said Monday. "And I think the biggest thing is the takeaways, the turnovers. We've got to do a great job of taking care of the football, especially in the red zone, when you've already got three points. You've got to be smart down there. Don't force anything. And I believe he'll do a great job of that moving forward."

Jones threw two interceptions in the redzone against Tennessee, helping the Titans erase a 13-0 deficit to record their first win after an 0-5 start. He has dealt with myriad issues this season, from his continued recovery from a torn Achilles last December, to his underwhelming receiving corps and inconsistent offensive-line play.

But Jones' dropoff from 2025, his best season, has been alarming. His completion percentage last season was a career-high 68%. This season, Jones is completing a career-low 59.6% of his attempts.

articles.headline: Can the Saints carry their winning momentum into Paris?
articles.description: After New Orleans snapped its three-game losing streak, the team's focus quickly turns to Week 7 in France.
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- Some of the New Orleans Saints didn't quite know what to make of their 34-27 win against the New York Giants on Sunday.

A video of Saints coach Kellen Moore's postgame speech showed the contrast. While players clapped and cheered as Moore handed out game balls, the overall atmosphere was subdued despite the win snapping a three-game losing streak.

The Saints got the job done, but it had taken a monumental effort for a game that seemed well in hand in the fourth quarter. The Saints had even started to pull a few starters when up 34-10 with 11:30 left to play, but a fumble by CJ Donaldson got the Giants back in the game. The Saints (2-4) allowed three touchdowns in the last seven minutes and had to make a stop at their own 14-yard line to secure the win.

"Most important thing in this league is that you got the win," Saints safety Justin Reid said. "I mean, this league is measured in wins and losses. It's not measured in scores. I thought that in a lot of ways, there's a lot of ways for us to continue to improve, but we showed up to the plate when we needed to and was able to close out a tough game. One of the big lessons that we can learn though is to continue to press the issue and not take our foot off the gas at any moment."

Saints guard and team captain David Edwards made a brief statement in the postgame locker room, imploring everyone to use the game as a starting point as they head into a second road game against the Pittsburgh Steelers in Paris (Sunday, 9:30 a.m. ET, NFL Network). The Saints flew to France immediately after the Giants game to get set up for the week ahead.

"We won this game because of our week of preparation and our mindset, period. How do we carry that moving forward? Positive, all together, that's who we are," Edwards said. "We showed that today, how do we build on that? That's our f---ing objective this week coming up. You got me?"

This week in France and Sunday's Week 7 game won't be without its own distractions. The NFL announced Sunday that the game is still scheduled as planned despite civil unrests and protests that have been happening over the past month in France.

Saints players said they had a security briefing before they left for Paris and will take precautions when sightseeing in the early part of the week.

Despite the outside disruptions, the Saints hope this week can be used as a "reset." Moore sees the trip as an opportunity for the players to spend more time together. "This is obviously a continuation of an extended trip going from New York to here," the coach said.

New Orleans is also banking on time away from home as a means to figure out why nothing, not even their two wins, have come easily. In Week 2, the Saints had to come back from an 11-point deficit to beat the Baltimore Ravens 24-17.

The Saints' issues on offense have been abundant: An inconsistent kicking game, a struggling run game and shaky offensive line play that resulted in quarterback Tyler Shough breakin

articles.headline: Mavericks waive center Dwight Powell after 12-year run
articles.description: The Mavericks waived longtime center Dwight Powell on Monday, likely ending his 12-year run with the franchise.
articles.body:
DALLAS -- The Dallas Mavericks waived longtime center Dwight Powell on Monday, likely ending his 12-year run with the franchise after he was the secondary piece in a trade that brought Rajon Rondo from Boston.

Powell was a late add just as training camp started last month, raising the possibility of a 13th season with the Mavericks. Dallas already had the full allotment of 15 guaranteed contracts, so keeping Powell would have forced the team to release one of those players.

The 35-year-old Powell was in and out of the rotation throughout his time with the Mavericks. He has played all but five of his 768 games with Dallas, including 266 starts. He has averaged 6.5 points, 4.2 rebounds and 17.5 minutes per game.

Powell joined the Mavericks in December 2014 when he and Rondo were part of a deal that included five players and two draft picks. Rondo and then-coach Rick Carlisle clashed, and Rondo left without playing a full season with Dallas. Powell played the next 11 full seasons with the Mavericks.

"Dwight was the consummate professional throughout his 12 seasons with the Mavericks and embodies everything you want in someone representing your organization," president of basketball operations Masai Ujiri said. "He's a tireless worker, an incredible teammate and someone whose impact extends well beyond the basketball court and into the Dallas community."

So far in Europe's top tournament, nine teams are a perfect 2-0-0 to open their campaign, though some of those teams -- Stuttgart! Real Betis! -- are flying higher than their league form should suggest. That said, there are several juggernauts crowded at the top end of the table and some true heavyweight clashes ahead this week, as Barcelona visit back-to-back champions Paris Saint-Germain on Tuesday and Bayern Munich welcome Premier League champions Arsenal to the Allianz Arena on Wednesday.

What will it do to the standings?

Throughout the competition, we will be asking our writers, editors and other experts to rank the top 10 teams in the tournament in terms of who they think are the strongest and most likely to win it all. Here are your Champions League Power Rankings going into a fun week.

UCL Power Rankings before Matchday 3

1. PARIS SAINT-GERMAIN

- Previous rank: 1

- Games since MD1: defeated Brest 1-0, defeated Marseille 2-1, defeated Le Mans 3-1, defeated Man City 4-2, defeated Strasbourg 3-1

- MD3 opponent: vs. Barcelona, Tuesday

Luis Enrique's side is a notorious slow starter domestically, by its own admission, but after two draws and a defeat to open the season, PSG well and truly seem back on track now. Since a 6-1 rout of Slovan Bratislava on UCL Matchday 1, they've won every game with a rotating cast of characters. Summer signing Ferran Torres from Barcelona has seven goals already, and 10 different players have found the net across the team's 11 games in all competitions.

Young arrivals Mika Godts and Maghnes Akliouche have also embraced Luis Enrique's style of play, and while PSG do look a little wobbly at the back with the veteran Marquinhos losing a step and goalie Matvey Safonov also fallible, they have the attacking prowess to make that less of an issue. articles.headline: Mayfield to practice this week but Buccaneers to prep as if Daniels will play
articles.description: Baker Mayfield will return to practice Wednesday for the Buccaneers, but the team will prepare as if Jalon Daniels will start at QB, coach Todd Bowles said.
articles.body:
TAMPA, Fla. -- Buccaneers starting quarterback Baker Mayfield will return to practice this week for the first time since suffering a dislocated right thumb, but Tampa Bay will prepare as if rookie Jalon Daniels will play Sunday against the Carolina Panthers, coach Todd Bowles said Monday.

"He's supposed to practice Wednesday," Bowles said Monday. "We're gonna take a good look at him there and then we'll kind of evaluate him during the week and see how he does."

The expectation was always that Mayfield would miss a minimum of three weeks after suffering his injury in Week 3.

He required stitches initially because of the way in which his thumb bent but did not undergo surgery. An MRI revealed no microfractures, tendon or ligament damage. He has now entered the early part of a potential window to return, but sources close to the situation say the key will be how well he is able to grip the football. And of course, that gripping action would be required over the course of an entire game. It's not just about gripping the ball but securing it, sources have said, while adding that pain is not currently an issue. 

As for how the team goes about preparing for the Panthers this week -- their first divisional opponent of the season after a 1-5 start -- Bowles explained why the team will prepare as if Daniels will make his fourth straight start.

"I think you have to," Bowles said. "They'll both be in the meetings and we'll see how the week goes before we decide who it is."

Daniels was able to secure the Buccaneers their first victory of the season -- a primetime win over the Dallas Cowboys in Week 5 but threw two interceptions in the fourth quarter in a 26-19 overtime loss to the Pittsburgh Steelers on Sunday. The Bucs struggled to establish a ground game and sustain drives in that contest, forcing Daniels into 43 passing attempts.

Daniels was then unable to match quarterback Aaron Rodgers' 6-yard touchdown pass to Germie Bernard with 3:20 to go in overtime. The game ended with Daniels being sacked on fourth down by an unaccounted-for Jalen Ramsey on a blitz. That's a situation where Mayfield's experience could have helped, but he struggled in the three games before sustaining the injury, throwing two touchdowns with a third on the ground, two interceptions, and he lost three fumbles. He was also sacked 13 times.

Is it possible the Bucs could change the trajectory of their season as divisional play begins? At 3-2, the Panthers are currently the only team in the NFC South with a winning record. Last season, the Bucs, Panthers and Atlanta Falcons all finished with losing records (8-9) but were tied atop the division, with Carolina advancing via a tiebreaker.

articles.headline: PSG-Barcelona Champions League match to go ahead despite France protests
articles.description: The showpiece UCL match between PSG and Barcelona will go ahead as planned on Tuesday in Paris despite a weekend of violent protests.
articles.body:
PARIS -- The showpiece Champions League match between Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona will go ahead as planned on Tuesday in the French capital city, the French Interior minister confirmed, despite a weekend of protests marred by violence and looting across the country.

Many French citizens have been left shocked by the images of violence that have drawn worldwide attention and highlighted the country's tense social climate. On Monday, French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said he has instructed prefects to impose "very limited" and "localized" curfews in cities to prevent more rioting and looting.

The violence targeted city halls, other public buildings and hundreds of businesses across the country, leading to more than 2,000 arrests.

Tuesday's match between PSG and Barcelona at the Parc des Princes will require a robust security deployment, with police forces already strained following weeks of student protests. In May, Paris police detained dozens of people after violence disrupted celebrations of PSG's second Champions League title win and a group tried to storm a police station in the French capital.

Speaking after an emergency meeting with top government officials, Interior minister Laurent Nuñez said the possibility of calling off planned events was discussed, including football matches.

"But this does not apply to tomorrow's match between PSG and FC Barcelona," he said, adding that other matches planned in European competitions this week would not be affected. Nuñez mentioned the match between Lille and Galatasaray scheduled Wednesday in the northern city, where looters also vandalized shops over the weekend.

Nuñez offered his resignation on Sunday but French President Emmanuel Macron asked him to stay to respond to police needs in an emergency situation. Macron instructed Nuñez "to take all necessary steps to ensure full transparency about the failures in planning and intelligence-gathering that led to the violence."

Lecornu said details of the areas to be placed under curfew will be provided later.

Nuñez acknowledged that authorities had "lost control" in some major cities on Saturday, with hundreds of businesses looted.

Cason Wallace terms: Five years, $139 million

Grade: B-

Wallace's contract, worth $27.8 million per year, is right in line with the going rate for young, defense-first perimeter players. Other recent rookie extensions include $31 million per year for Ausar Thompson, $30 million per year for Jalen Suggs and $25 million per year for Dyson Daniels.

Granted, the extensions for Suggs and Daniels haven't aged especially well since they were signed, given both players' offensive regressions.

There's good reason for the Thunder to believe Wallace is worth this contract, however, in a vacuum: A second-team All-Defensive honoree last season with one of the highest annual steal rates, he's one of the NBA's best perimeter stoppers, and he seems to have yet-untapped offensive potential, as well. He has never averaged more than 8.6 points in a season, but he's a career 37% 3-point shooter. And over a 15-game stretch last winter, mostly with Shai Gilgeous-Alexander sidelined, Wallace averaged 13.9 points and 4.7 assists while assuming much greater offensive responsibilities.

The Thunder are betting there's more where that burst came from, now that Wallace is presumably set to take Luguentz Dort's spot in the starting lineup. He can defend most of the same stars Dort used to guard, while adding more offensive oomph and playmaking against elite defenses. In the conference finals against San Antonio, for example, Dort averaged 4.3 points and made 20% of his 3s, while Wallace averaged 10.1 points and made 50% of his 3s.

But this extension doesn't come in a vacuum; rather, it comes amid a threatening financial backdrop for Oklahoma City, which already had to trade Dort, Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe this summer for financial reasons. And the purse strings could get even tighter next year, when Gilgeous-Alexander's supermax extension kicks in.

To that end, one of the most important executive quotes of this summer came from the Thunder's Sam Presti, who told Justin Martinez of The Oklahoman, "The impression I have been given is that the savings generated this summer, and from being out of the tax the last several years, will be reallocated to future teams."

Those savings will need to be reallocated for Wallace's extension

articles.headline: Ugonna Onyenso thought his NBA dream was over -- then the Detroit Pistons called him up
articles.description: Detroit Pistons center Ugonna Onyenso was surprised to hear his name called out 53rd at the 2026 NBA Draft, having once believed his dream of making the league was over, but is now confident he can grow into the sizable shoes left by Isaiah Stewart.
